standard.title: Textiles — Polypropylene Spun Bonded Non-Woven Crop Covers and Fruit Skirting Bags for Agricultural and Horticultural Applications — Specification (First Revision)
standard.sector: Technical Textiles / Technical Textiles for Agrotech Applications

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Agrotech Applications Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the physical, mechanical, and performance requirements, along with corresponding test methods, for crop covers and fruit skirting bags manufactured from UV-stabilized polypropylene spun-bonded non-woven fabrics. These technical textiles are designed for agricultural and horticultural crop protection to create a beneficial micro-climate, shield delicate plants and fruits from frost, wind, birds, and insect infestations, and reduce chemical pesticide dependency while maximizing crop yields.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all Crop Covers and Fruit Skirting Bags manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 16718:2021 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified crop covers or fruit skirting bags is a statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic spun-bonded agricultural non-wovens.
requirements: Every roll or bundle of certified crop covers and skirting bags must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 16718) on a secure label or edge tape.

The non-woven fabric must be manufactured from 100% virgin polypropylene (PP) spun-bonded filaments. The use of recycled or scrap polymer blends that would compromise tensile strength or environmental safety is strictly prohibited.

The standard classifies products into two main types based on application: a) Crop Covers (Type I): lightweight sheets designed to create a greenhouse effect on seedbeds; b) Fruit Skirting Bags (Type II): pre-cut protective bags designed for wrapping developing fruit bunches.

The standard variety weights are established for agricultural consistency: a) Type I (Crop Covers) is typically specified at 17 g/m² (GSM); b) Type II (Fruit Skirting Bags) is typically specified at 22 g/m² (GSM). Custom weights can be declared by the manufacturer as agreed.
To guarantee adequate physical protection and insulation, the minimum fabric thickness must be strictly verified: minimum 0.18 mm for both Type I and Type II variants.

To withstand strong field winds, rain, and manual tensioning over supporting hoops, the fabric must demonstrate high breaking strength in both Machine Direction (MD) and Cross Direction (CD) when tested per IS 15891 (Part 3).

The spun-bonded web must resist localized tearing and punctures from sharp branches or installation stakes, satisfying specified minimum trapezoid tear strength limits (MD and CD) when tested per IS 15891 (Part 4).

To ensure proper ventilation and prevent hot air pockets or suffocating micro-climates, the fabric must satisfy strict minimum air permeability limits: minimum 400 cm³/cm²/s for Type I (17 GSM) and minimum 350 cm³/cm²/s for Type II (22 GSM) when tested per IS 15891 (Part 15).

To prevent excessive humidity build-up and fungal condensation under the sheet, the fabric must satisfy a high water vapour transmission rate: minimum 800 g/m²/day for both Type I and Type II when tested per the dish method of Annex B.

To guarantee an outdoor service life of multiple seasons under intense solar exposure, the fabric must undergo 144 hours of accelerated UV exposure (using a fluorescent UV-B 313 nm lamp per Annex C) and maintain a high percentage of its initial breaking strength (typically at least 50% or more).

Where a manufacturer claims oxo-biodegradability for eco-friendly landfill disposal, the polymer must incorporate suitable pro-oxidant catalysts. The composite fabric must demonstrate abiotic degradation—breaking down physically within 144 hours of UV exposure.
